clue.text: She once wrote up drivers, or the author, with Word help

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to herself or himself as me
a term is a word
aid is help

explanation.surface: A woman writer of the past, a motoring author and a word processor's help screen jostle in one sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She once wrote' suggests a famous author, but this is a traffic warden writing parking tickets; 'once' because the job title is now old-fashioned. 'Word' is not Microsoft's program, just a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A meter maid was a female traffic officer who issued tickets to motorists parked at expired meters.

clue.text: Rock is manlier if out of control

indicators.note: something out of control runs wild, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A rock musician turns more macho when things get wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests rock music or steadiness, but it is a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock is a solid natural substance made of one or more minerals, a loose synonym.

clue.text: Generates chaos for youths

indicators.note: chaos throws things into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Adolescents are a source of mayhem, as any parent knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are young people aged thirteen to nineteen, the plural of a youth.

clue.text: Crazy myth underlies factor in blood and pulse

indicators.note: in a down entry, what lies under another piece comes after it

parts.note: the Rh (rhesus) factor is a blood protein

indicators.note: crazy means wild and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A wild legend about blood and the heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is a regular beat, and rhythm is a regular repeated pattern of beats.

clue.text: Head count at Hamilton cotillion

parts.note: taken as written
Alexander Hamilton's portrait is on the US ten-dollar bill
a cotillion is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Someone counts the guests at a ball held by the Hamiltons.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Hamilton' is American slang for a ten-dollar bill, which bears his face.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance is the number of people present at an event, found by counting heads.

clue.text: Read translation for an alternative to truth

indicators.note: a translation turns words into another form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Reading a translation is offered instead of the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'truth' sounds like honesty, but the definition is the party game Truth or Dare.
explanation.definitionFit: In the game Truth or Dare a player who will not answer a question must take a dare instead.

clue.text: Poke around company with twin

indicators.note: around says one word wraps itself about the other, holding it inside

parts.note: to jab is to poke
Co. is the standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Someone nudges a business partner who happens to be a twin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poke around' looks like a single verb meaning snoop, but 'around' is the container signal acting on Poke.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob is the twin brother of Esau, so he is the classic biblical example of a twin.

clue.text: Convergence of Jewish initiation and the act of anointing

indicators.note: an initiation is a beginning, so take only the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of this word
unction is anointing with oil, as in a religious rite

explanation.surface: A religious ceremony brings together Jewish initiation rites and anointing with oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jewish initiation' suggests a bar mitzvah, but initiation here means the word's beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A junction is a place where roads or lines meet, a point of convergence.

clue.text: I'm involved in gang, mostly for arson or loan-sharking

indicators.note: something involved in a group is placed inside it
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a crew is a gang
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A mobster admits joining a gang that deals in arson and loan-sharking.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson and loan-sharking are both examples of illegal acts, so each is a crime.

clue.text: One looking through a book to live right when having spats

indicators.note: having something means holding it, so one part takes in the other

parts.note: to be is to live, to exist
R is the abbreviation for right
rows are quarrels, spats

explanation.surface: A reader tries to live properly amid quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spats' could be old-fashioned shoe coverings; here they are quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser idly leafs through a book or shop, glancing rather than reading closely.

clue.text: Every other element in niece's day is lacking

indicators.note: every other element means take one letter, skip one, take the next, and so on

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of these words

explanation.surface: A niece is having a day when every other thing is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy describes someone poor, short of the necessities of life, which is to be lacking.

clue.text: Film director, ragin', gets in the way?

indicators.note: something that gets in is placed inside something else

parts.note: the Tao is the Way of Chinese philosophy
ranting is raging, and the apostrophe drops the final G here too

explanation.surface: A furious film director is obstructing everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in the way' reads as obstructing, but it is the instruction to put one word inside TAO. Quentin Tarantino is the American director of Pulp Fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is an American who directs films, such as Pulp Fiction and Kill Bill.

clue.text: Coming to, and feeling pain again?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
aching is feeling pain

explanation.surface: Someone regains consciousness, only to find that it hurts once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to' looks like waking up, but it means arriving at a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching a place is arriving at it, which is coming to it.

clue.text: In Europe, capital "A"s?

wordplay.note: read the letter A followed by an S as A, then S

explanation.surface: A question about capital letters A written by Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' seems to describe the letter as upper case; it is a capital city. The plural A's is spelt out as A, then S.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece, a European country.

clue.text: Definitely, Coke is spilled in space alien's orifices

indicators.note: in says one set of letters goes inside another

parts.note: E.T. is the film's space alien, and the 's adds S
yes is an emphatic agreement, definitely

indicators.note: a spilled drink spreads in a jumble, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Spilling a soft drink on an alien's face, absurdly, lands it in the eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: E.T. is the alien of Spielberg's 1982 film. 'Definitely' looks like an opening adverb but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye sockets are the openings in the skull that hold the eyes, so they are cavities or orifices.

clue.text: Herb to reveal a secret on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so a word spelt differently can sound the same

parts.note: to leak is to reveal a secret

explanation.surface: Someone spills confidential information over the airwaves, with a herb mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb here is used loosely for a green culinary plant, as American cookbooks sometimes do.
explanation.definitionFit: The leek is an edible plant of the onion family, a green culinary plant like chives.

clue.text: Someone who's probably about to retire with a firecracker?

definitions.text: Someone who's probably about to retire
definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone born in the post-war birth surge, now reaching retirement age

definitions.note: the answer read as a small banger
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: an infant boomer, a little thing that goes bang

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, whimsical reading: a boomer is something that booms, and a baby one is a small firecracker.
explanation.definitionFit: Baby boomers were born from 1946 to 1964, so in 2015 many were nearing retirement age.

clue.text: It might blow one mutant to pieces

indicators.note: blown to pieces, the letters scatter and are put back in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A bomb that might blow a mutant creature apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' suggests an explosion; the definition is a volcano erupting.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna in Sicily is an active volcano, which can erupt, or blow its top.

clue.text: Stuck with what some did on Yom Kippur?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stuck firmly in place

definitions.text: what some did on Yom Kippur?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split: observed a day without food

explanation.walkthrough: Yom Kippur, the Jewish Day of Atonement, is a fast day; the question mark warns the phrase is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Held fast means gripped firmly, unable to move, which is to be stuck.

clue.text: Dysfunctional person to luxuriate, and so forth, beside stormy sea

parts.note: to bask is to luxuriate, as in the sun

indicators.note: stormy water is churned up, so these letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: etc. is the abbreviation for et cetera, and so forth
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A troubled person lounges about, doing this and that, by a rough sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket case is slang for someone too nervous or troubled to function properly.

clue.text: Alibi (a frantic cover) for certain inhabitant of Nigeria

indicators.note: these words act as a cover, concealing the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the a, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A panicked suspect concocts a cover story about a Nigerian.
explanation.walkthrough: Biafra was the south-eastern region of Nigeria that tried to break away in 1967 to 1970.
explanation.definitionFit: A Biafran lives in the Biafra region of Nigeria, so is one particular kind of Nigerian.

clue.text: Big show of affection at the end of squabble

parts.note: a hug is a show of affection

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Two people make up with a big embrace after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big show of affection' reads as one phrase, but 'Big' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge is a synonym for very large in size, the same as big.

clue.text: Former spouse crept stealthily in passage

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife

indicators.note: moving stealthily is sneaking about, so these letters move into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A former spouse sneaked quietly along a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' paints a corridor; here it is a piece of text.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a short extract from a book or piece of music, a passage taken from it.

clue.text: Suit canceled in outback

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: split into out plus back, with back telling us to read out backwards
x'd, crossed out with an X, is canceled

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is dropped somewhere in the Australian bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outback' looks like Australia's interior; split it into out and back. The outback is Australia's remote inland.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuxedo is a man's formal dinner suit.

clue.text: Give a prosecutor weapons and a bunch of ships

parts.note: to arm someone is to give them weapons
taken as written
a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
no letters of its own: it completes the phrase give weapons that the first piece stands for

explanation.surface: Arming a lawyer and handing over a fleet sound like a strange government decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give a prosecutor weapons' is read as give weapons (ARM), then A, then the prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, a crowd of vessels sailing together.

clue.text: City in Georgia or Massachusetts supported by swindle

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is supported sits on top, so it comes first

parts.note: MA is the postal abbreviation for Massachusetts
a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A quiz asks which state a city is in, Georgia or Massachusetts.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface offers a choice of two states; one is the definition, the other is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Macon is a city in central Georgia, in the southern United States.

clue.text: A mixed stucco outside facade of Institute of Sound

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: outside says one set of letters goes round the other
mixed means stirred up, its letters jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

indicators.note: the facade of a building is its front, so take only the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A building institute of sound engineering has its frontage covered in plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Institute of Sound' reads as a name, but 'of Sound' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acoustic means relating to sound or hearing, so it is an adjective for 'of sound'.

clue.text: Old painter turned up after taking Sunday off

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top
taking off a day's abbreviation removes that letter from the word

parts.note: Edgar Degas was the French Impressionist who painted ballet dancers

explanation.surface: An elderly artist got up after a day off on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the abbreviation for Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, having lived a long time, so it is a synonym of old.

clue.text: Edges away from accident and snarl in square, for instance

indicators.note: with the edges taken away, the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: a wreck is an accident, as on the road
a snarl is a tangle, as in a snarled rope

explanation.surface: A traffic accident causes a snarl-up in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarl in square' paints gridlock in a plaza; 'in' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A square is one example of a rectangle, a four-sided figure with right angles.

clue.text: Tenant arrives late with a key

indicators.note: one who arrives late misses the start, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a renter is a tenant

explanation.surface: A tenant shows up late, key in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The tenant's key looks like a door key, but the definition is a keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: Enter is the name of a computer keyboard key, the one pressed to confirm a line.

clue.text: Muses, for example, defining attribute of a risky aerial act

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of nine, as the Muses of Greek myth are

definitions.text: defining attribute of a risky aerial act
definitions.note: read as the two words no net
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two: a trapeze act is risky when it has no safety net

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is read as two words, the absence of a safety net under a trapeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a set of nine, and there were nine Muses in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Prince William and offspring of a queen are not in harmony

parts.note: Prince William is Diana's son, read as DI'S SON
every worker ant is born to the colony's queen

explanation.surface: Prince William and the Queen's other descendants are quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Di is Diana, Princess of Wales. 'offspring of a queen' points at the royals, but the queen is a queen ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissonant music has clashing notes, so it is without harmony; figuratively it means at odds.
